`PropTypes.any`, `PropTypes.array`, and `PropTypes.object` check almost nothing. `users: PropTypes.array` accepts an array of anything, so React never warns about a bad item. `arrayOf`, `objectOf`, and `shape` say what's inside.

{/* Generated by src/codegen/lint-rule-docs.ts. Do not edit this section. */}

## Configure

Off by default. To turn it on:

```toml bunfig.toml
[lint.rules]
"react/forbid-prop-types" = "error" # or "warn"
```

Every option, set to its default:

```toml bunfig.toml
[lint.rules]
"react/forbid-prop-types" = ["error", {
  forbid = ["any", "array", "object"],
  checkContextTypes = false,
  checkChildContextTypes = false,
}]
```

{/* End of the generated section. */}

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad */}
```jsx
import PropTypes from "prop-types";

function UserList({ users }) {
  return <ul>{users.map(user => <li key={user.id}>{user.name}</li>)}</ul>;
}

UserList.propTypes = {
  users: PropTypes.array.isRequired,
};
```

The rule also looks inside `shape({ ... })` and at the arguments of a prop type:

{/* bad {"count": 2} */}
```jsx
import PropTypes from "prop-types";

function Card({ tags, owner }) {
  return <div title={owner.name}>{tags.length}</div>;
}

Card.propTypes = {
  tags: PropTypes.arrayOf(PropTypes.object),
  owner: PropTypes.shape({ name: PropTypes.any }),
};
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```jsx
import PropTypes from "prop-types";

function UserList({ users }) {
  return <ul>{users.map(user => <li key={user.id}>{user.name}</li>)}</ul>;
}

UserList.propTypes = {
  users: PropTypes.arrayOf(
    PropTypes.shape({ id: PropTypes.number, name: PropTypes.string }),
  ).isRequired,
};
```

## Options

| Option | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `forbid` | `["any", "array", "object"]` | The prop types to report. Your list replaces the default one. |
| `checkContextTypes` | `false` | Also check `contextTypes`. |
| `checkChildContextTypes` | `false` | Also check `childContextTypes`. |

With `forbid: ["any"]`, `object` is allowed and `any` is still reported:

{/* bad {"options": [{"forbid": ["any"]}], "count": 1} */}
```jsx
import PropTypes from "prop-types";

function Card({ style, extra }) {
  return <div style={style}>{extra}</div>;
}

Card.propTypes = {
  style: PropTypes.object,
  extra: PropTypes.any,
};
```

{/* bad {"options": [{"checkContextTypes": true}]} */}
```jsx
import PropTypes from "prop-types";

function Title(props, context) {
  return <h1 style={context.theme}>{props.text}</h1>;
}

Title.contextTypes = {
  theme: PropTypes.object,
};
```

## When not to use it

React 19 ignores `propTypes`. If you type your props with TypeScript instead, you don't need this rule.
